validation_scope: Learn a discrete graph-action world-model candidate from real Phase9 compact/micro/V3 transition outcomes.  It uses a redacted Boolean feature snapshot and leave-one-out candidate policy evaluation.  Teacher distillation is reported only as a bootstrap upper bound, not as independent world-model performance.

literature_design_basis.discrete_world_models_via_regularization: Boolean latent state, decorrelated bits, and sparse action-change framing motivate the redacted graph-action feature representation.
literature_design_basis.dreamer_v2_v3: The world model is used for policy/search control over compact latent transitions rather than full observation reconstruction.
literature_design_basis.causal_world_models_for_language_agents: State and action variables remain language-facing and auditable instead of hidden prompt rules.
literature_design_basis.web_agents_with_world_models: The model predicts transition outcomes for decision support, matching transition-focused agent world-model practice.

calibrated_residual_guard.input_scope: redacted state_bits only; no prompts, answers, gold labels, or judge text at runtime

guard_rules.reason: High-frequency scaling examples need the full-context baseline unless validated otherwise.
Counterexample and safety repair cases prefer compact explicit failure framing.
Hard constraint tradeoffs prefer the micro guard's concise constraint handling.
Formal, generic review, and propulsion optimization boundaries abstain to the full baseline.

calibrated_residual_guard.interpretation: The raw reward predictor remains uncalibrated, but a bounded residual guard can safely combine it with previously validated Phase9 boundary cues.

model.state_representation: Redacted Boolean/tag latent vector over route, domain, pattern, and safe trigger bits.
model.learner: leave-one-out bucket estimator over shared latent bits with compact-action support rows

limitations: The raw outcome-only selector improves original V3 on this heldout slice but remains weaker than the retained hybrid guard.
The calibrated residual guard beats the retained hybrid on this slice, but it is still a bounded policy guard, not a full task-world simulator.
Scalar reward calibration for the raw predictor is still not better than a per-arm base-rate predictor, so raw predictions must not replace live ablation.
The compact support rows observe compact-action outcomes only and are used as support evidence, not as full V3/V1 labels.
interpretation: The raw outcome-only discrete world-model candidate improves original V3 on the Phase9 heldout slice (all-policy lift +0.0185; candidate lift +0.0588) while staying below the retained hybrid guard (gap -0.0370).  The calibrated residual guard repairs that gap (lift over retained hybrid +0.0186) without using raw prompts or answers, so the guard is promotable while the raw reward predictor remains a candidate.
